newsitem.title: USA: Skin substitute now available for burn victims.
newsitem.headline: Skin substitute now available for burn victims.

text.p: Burn victims will now be able to get a new temporary skin substitute while they wait for a skin graft, health officials said Wednesday
The Food and Drug Administration said it had approved a temporary skin called Dermagraft-TC, developed by Advanced Tissue Sciences of La Jolla, Calif.

There are other skin substitutes but Dermagraft is different because it uses human cells. The cells are grown in a lab on a nylon mesh, and then frozen. The freezing kills the cells but leaves intact a tissue matrix and cell growth factors.
The surgeon unfreezes the patch, which is about 5 by 7 1/2 inches, and stretches it over the burn site until the patient is ready for a graft. That usually takes a week or two, the FDA said.
The company had announced the FDA approval late Tuesday and said Dermagraft-TC is available to burn centers across the country.
About 51,000 Americans are hospitalized for severe burns each year, and about 5,500 of them die. Wounds must be covered quickly to prevent infection and minimize scarring.
